item.title: How to influence political decisions on Sweden's new citizenship rules
item.description: A number of The Local's readers have reached out since more details of the planned changes to Swedish citizenship rules were unveiled in February asking how they can share their opinions with decision-makers. Here are a few ways to do so.

item.title: Why a legal watchdog slammed Sweden's citizenship plan
item.description: In this week's podcast: three years of teen deportations, legal experts blast lack of transitional rules for citizenship applicants, Swedish birthday traditions, and how Sweden is restricting immigrants' access to welfare benefits.

item.title: They contribute to Swedish society: now the government is changing the rules
item.description: Naval architects, fundraising experts, doctors, software engineers, tech entrepreneurs, executive management consultants: meet the people reconsidering their lives and careers in Sweden as a result of the government’s new citizenship laws.

item.title: INSIDE SWEDEN: Why it's crunch time for foreigners' migration rights in March
item.description: In this week's Inside Sweden newsletter The Local's Nordic Editor Richard Orange runs through the massive amount of migration news in the pipeline in March, and then rounds up the week's stories.

item.title: Culture, politics, food: what makes Europeans proud of their country?
item.description: A recent survey by the Pew Research Centre delved into what people feel proudest about in their country, with Europeans pointing to history, food and culture among the main reasons.

item.title: Sweden confirms Russian drone buzzed French aircraft carrier in Malmö
item.description: The Swedish military confirmed Friday that a drone jammed near a French aircraft carrier this week was Russian as France slammed the spy attempt as a "ridiculous provocation".

item.title: When is Sweden's parliament set to vote on new migration laws?

item.title: UPDATED: What does Sweden's plan to restrict benefits for newcomers mean for work permit holders?
item.description: Sweden is pushing forward with new rules which will make it harder for foreigners to qualify for social insurance, including parental benefits and child support, with the government set to publish a draft bill proposing tougher rules.
